At night, it’s worse. I fall asleep okay, but I keep jolting awake, heart racing, drenched in sweat. Sometimes I’m not even sure where I am for a few seconds. It’s been nearly every night. I’ve been short-tempered, can’t focus during safety briefings, and I keep canceling layovers because being on a plane now just makes me panic.

D019-D018_h016.question_both:
I’ve been off ever since it happened. I can’t drive past the intersection where the accident took place—just seeing that stretch of road makes my chest tighten and my hands sweat, even if I’m not the one driving. Sometimes my heart starts racing for no reason, like my body remembers something my mind won’t show me. I don’t remember much from that night, not really. It’s like a blank spot—flashes of headlights, then nothing until I’m in the ambulance. The rest is fog.

I’ve stopped going to client meetings in that part of town. I make excuses, reschedule, anything to avoid it. Even talking about cars or insurance claims lately… it just gets to me. My ex asked why I’ve been so distant, but I can’t explain it. I don’t want to think about it, let alone talk. But it’s not like it’s every second of the day. Some days are okay. Others, a sound—like screeching tires or a slamming door—and I’m right back there, or at least partway.

It’s only been… I don’t know, a few weeks? Maybe less. Time’s been blurry. I don’t know if I’m overreacting or if this is normal. I just know I can’t go back to that place, and I can’t remember what happened—even though part of me feels like I should.
D019-D018_h016.question_a:
I’ve been struggling ever since the car accident three weeks ago—just me, stopped at a red light, and then out of nowhere, a pickup truck slammed into my car. I remember the sound, that awful crunch, and then waking up in the hospital with a neck brace, but I can’t piece together most of what happened in the minutes before impact. It’s like a blank.  

Since then, every time I hear a sudden noise—like a car door slamming or brakes squealing—my heart races, I sweat, and I feel like I can’t breathe. I’ve had to stop taking calls from clients in parking lots because just being near traffic brings it all back. I even switched routes to avoid the intersection where it happened. I’m supposed to go back to work full time, but I just can’t bring myself to drive there.  

I haven’t told anyone much about it—my ex asked, and I shut down. I don’t want to talk about it, see anything about car crashes online, or even sit in the passenger seat. It’s been about three weeks now, and I keep hoping it’ll pass, but I’m not getting better yet.
D019-D018_h016.question_b:
I’ve been having these overwhelming reactions ever since the car accident back in March—almost four months ago now. It was bad; I remember sirens, glass shattering, and then waking up in the hospital with no memory of how I got there. To this day, I can’t piece together most of what happened during the crash. Sometimes, if I hear a sudden loud noise, like a truck backfiring or even a car horn, my heart starts racing, I sweat, and I feel like I can’t breathe—like I’m right back in that moment.

I used to drive all over the city meeting clients, but now I avoid getting behind the wheel. I’ve turned down meetings if they’re too far or in busy areas. I even skip certain roads I used to take all the time. If someone brings up accidents or insurance claims related to car crashes, I change the subject or step away. It’s affecting my work—clients are noticing.

I didn’t think it would last this long. I figured after a few weeks I’d bounce back, but here I am, still jumpy, still avoiding things, still not remembering. It’s been more than a month now, and honestly, some days feel worse than when it first happened.
